review: Wren's round-156 request (Practical root cooking: prepare an owned meadow root into a cooked meal with explicit material, heat and energy requirements, no assumed fuel, tools or heat, no guaranteed improvement) received the World Agent decision develop (learning 3): a general thermal food preparation with modes prepare-hearth, ignite, tend, cook, inspect, retrieve, extinguish and cancel, a minimal physically gated hand-friction fire, the smallest dry-roasting process without pot, water or metal tools, one whole root per trial, conservative nutrition, unchanged spoilage and eat path, and no reward. The specification is self-consistent, so this is not a first release: implemented hearth-food-preparation@1 (scope long-ex17, ability hearth-food-preparation, handler long.hearth-food-preparation; renamed from an earlier draft id so that revisions, handlers and exports stay unique beside the separate long-ex18 thermal-food-preparation@1 package). Existing fire representations were searched first: local-fire@1 (forest-fire.ts, a stone hearth, friction kit, combustion and warming of people tied to thermal-refuge satisfaction) is not installed in long-ex17 and stays byte-identical; its values are reused here without its satisfaction trigger, warming or reward. prepare-hearth: two paid rounds of 1 energy clear a 0.45 m bare bed (local-fire footprint) on meadow, dry or forest ground that is not water, a ford, wet or saturated soil, under open sky, 0.7 m clear of objects, loose items and people (local-fire clearance); no stack is created; the hearth object has createdBy null so observers see only its public mode and progress. tend: 1 round, 0.5 energy, moves owned branch, bark or dry grass (the local-fire fuel set, tenths, bed capacity 8 mass) from inventory onto the bed and/or turns the cook's own food. ignite: needs an unlit hearth loaded with at least 0.5 dry grass tinder and 0.5 branch kindling, an owned whole board of soft wood (branch or willow, hardness at most 3) and an owned whole spindle of a harder wood (birch or oak), all at moisture at most 0.35, rain at most 0.15 and wind at most 0.65 (local-fire ignition limits); pieces are reserved, carried and returned worn with a recorded socket and worn mass; up to 12 drilling rounds of 1.5 energy are paid only when performed, then an ember transfer round and a first tending round of 0.5 energy each, burning 0.1 dry grass each; an ember not worked in the next round dies; failure after 12 rounds leaves worn pieces, drill dust as hearth residue and no fire. Combustion reuses local-fire@1 rules as values: at most 1 fuel unit per round times (1 - moisture), per-unit fuel values from the resource table, 10% ash and 90% released gases, embers three rounds after the last burn, rain above 0.6 douses it; loose fuel lying within 0.25 m of a lit bed catches and joins it. cook: 1 round, 0.5 energy, lays exactly one whole owned unspoiled root or berry (foods whose water composition the world represents) on the bed, reserved and owned by nobody, so it cannot be eaten, planted, given or cooked elsewhere; one portion per hearth; on a bed above 60 C placing, turning and retrieving need an owned whole branch as a stick (not consumed); retrieve takes the food by hand only when its surface is at most 50 C and the bed at most 60 C, otherwise the stick rakes it aside to cool in air; extinguish (1 round, 0.5 energy) smothers the fire with the soil cleared from the bed, leaving unburned fuel; inspect (1 round, 0.2 energy) records the perceivable hearth, fuel wetness and food surface condition plus a model estimate of rounds and fuel to the cooked criterion as an unverified personal record, never the core temperature, or checks up to four owned items by touch; cancel (no energy) ends unfinished clearing or drilling and returns reserved pieces once; death drops them where the person died while fire and food continue. Events: hearth-work-progress, hearth-prepared, hearth-work-paused, hearth-work-resumed, hearth-work-cancelled, friction-progress, friction-ember-formed, friction-ember-died, friction-ignition-failed, hearth-ember-transferred, hearth-ignited, hearth-fed, hearth-fuel-burned, hearth-extinguished, hearth-material-caught, hearth-food-placed, hearth-food-turned, hearth-food-changed, hearth-food-raked, hearth-food-retrieved, hearth-inspected; practice evidence is the retrieval event, which never carries a qualified flag, so cooking earns no milestone. The cooked unit keeps its identity, origin, harvest date and decay and keeps ageing under the unchanged rule; its char is scraped off as hearth residue; it eats through the unchanged eat handler as one unit at its original nutrition times its remaining unburnt solids share (never above 14 per root, never more for water loss), through the existing per-stack food-profile hook, which is read only for this record in worlds with this operation installed and gives no new meal method or quality, so no meal-variety or pleasure change; whole units are required because the existing eat path in this world consumes whole units only. Modeling assumptions (declared, not discovered facts): thermal time of one round is 18 minutes (one eightieth of the 80-round day), used only inside the heat integration; 1 local-fire fuel unit releases 2 MJ (a 1.1 kg branch holds 8 units, about 16 MJ of air-dry wood), which overstates light fuels such as dry grass and bark because their existing per-unit fuel values are kept; fuel and wood moisture follows the local-fire rule (current rain when untracked, +0.08*rain per rainy round outdoors, else -0.01*(1+wind)); hand drill 20 W at the contact, dust heat-loss conductance 0.04 W/K raised by half the wind, dryness factor 1 - moisture/0.35, socket warm-up 15 K per consecutive worked round, ember at 350 C with 2 g of dust, socket abrasion 1.5 mm per round with full contact at 3 mm, board wear 1.5 g and spindle wear 0.5 g per round; bed of about 5 kg soil and ash with heat capacity 4 kJ/K and loss 3 W/K to the surroundings (about 600 K above ambient at the full burn rate); food as a 1000 kg/m3 sphere split into two 15% faces and a 70% core, root water fraction 0.75 from the existing food water representation, heat capacity 4.18 kJ/kg/K for water and 1.5 for dry matter, bed contact coefficient 15 W/m2K on the lower face, still air 10 W/m2K, conductivity 0.5 W/m/K over half the radius, evaporation at 100 C with 2.26 MJ/kg, charring of dry tissue above 200 C at 2e-5 per K per second with 30% char yield and 70% gases, no moisture migration, shrinkage or char insulation; labels: cooked when the core has been at least 85 C for a cumulative 10 minutes, charred at 20% of solids burnt, destroyed below 10% remaining solids, with no claim of nutritional improvement, safety, detoxification, sterilization or longer shelf life. Heat and mass are ledgered exactly: released fire heat equals bed storage plus loss to the surroundings plus heat delivered to food, food heat equals its enthalpy change plus losses to air, vapour and pyrolysis gases, and food mass equals remaining water, solids and char plus evaporated water and gases; fuel burned equals ash plus released gases. Not modeled: warming or burning of people (the bed is solid and hot handling is blocked rather than injuring), ignition of vegetation (excluded by the placement clearance), other ignition routes or heat sources (no sun, sparks or spontaneous ignition), vessels, water, racks and multi-portion cooking. Reuse: local-fire@1 values and hearthSpatial, forestFireFuel, the food water composition, collective-work escrow and paid work, open-foundation personal records, unchanged gather, pickup, drop and eat. A new open-hearth drawing shows only actual state (dashed while cleared, fuel, drill during friction, glow only for embers, flame only while burning, smoke only with combustion, food colored by its modeled state). Current ex17 weather note from the frozen climate formula: at round 156 rain is about 0.8 and stays above 0.15 until about round 232, while wind stays below 0.65 until about round 296, so friction ignition is physically gated to that calm, dry window with material gathered after the rain or kept dry; in the tests, dry pieces in a calm warm spell form an ember on the second drilling round and pieces kept at moisture 0.34 fail after 12 rounds.
